# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tanaka_2026_vancomycin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tanaka_2026_vancomycin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s11095-026-04145-w> (open access; the
  electronic supplementary material holds supplementary Tables S1-S4, Figures
  S1-S6 and the final NONMEM control stream)

Tanaka 2026 is a retrospective population PK analysis of routine vancomycin
therapeutic drug monitoring in Japanese children. Its question is whether a
febrile state changes vancomycin clearance beyond what renal function explains.
The final model says it does: clearance is 27% higher on days when the daily
maximum body temperature reaches 38 degC, independently of the modified-Schwartz
eGFR. The paper then turns the model into a dose table (Table IV): for each age
group, eGFR band and temperature stratum, the daily dose in 5 mg/kg steps that
maximises the probability of an AUC from 48 to 72 h between 400 and
600 ug*h/mL. This vignette reproduces the clearance equation exactly and
re-derives Table IV from the packaged model.

# Population

The model was fit to 214 serum vancomycin concentrations from 129 inpatients
younger than 18 years treated in the Department of Pediatrics at Oita University
Hospital, Japan, between April 2011 and March 2021 (Tanaka 2026 Table I). 52.7%
were male. Age spanned the whole paediatric range: under 1 month 6.2%, 1 to
<3 months 5.4%, 3 to <12 months 10.1%, 1 to <6 years 27.9%, 6 to <12 years
25.6% and 12 to <18 years 24.8%. Median body weight was 16.9 kg (IQR 9.3-28.8),
height 104.0 cm (IQR 73.5-138.5), postmenstrual age 6.8 years (IQR 2.0-12.2) and
modified-Schwartz eGFR 118.4 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (IQR 96.8-151.9), with 26.4% of
patients above 150 mL/min/1.73 m^2. The cohort was febrile: median daily
maximum body temperature 38.6 degC (IQR 37.7-39.3), 30.2% met the paper's
febrile-neutropenia definition, and MRSA was cultured in 14.7%. Patients on
renal replacement therapy and those with an eGFR of 400 mL/min/1.73 m^2 or more
were excluded. Most samples were troughs and 54.3% of patients contributed a
single concentration, which is why the distribution parameters were fixed to
literature values rather than estimated.

The same information is available programmatically via the model's `population`
metadata (`readModelDb("Tanaka_2026_vancomycin")()$population`).

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries its source as an in-file comment in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Tanaka_2026_vancomycin.R`. The published control
stream (supplement 2) holds initial estimates only; the final values come from
Table III and supplement Table S3.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` | log(6.50) L/h | Table III theta_CL = 6.50 (RSE 5.0%); Results "6.50 L/h/70 kg" |
| `ltmat50` | log(49.1) weeks | Table III theta_TM50 = 49.1 weeks (RSE 8.5%) |
| `lhill_mat` | log(2.17) | Table III theta_Hill = 2.17 (RSE 14.7%) |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 0.423 | Table III theta_eGFR = 0.423 (RSE 27.7%) |
| `e_bodytemp_febrile_cl` | 1.27 | Table III theta_BT38 = 1.27 (RSE 3.8%); Results "CL increased by 27%" |
| `lvc` | log(39.9) L, held constant | Table III Vc = 39.9 L/70 kg, no RSE; Methods: taken from Le 2013 and Kloprogge 2019 |
| `lq` | log(3.85) L/h, held constant | Table III Q = 3.85 L/h/70 kg, no RSE; same Methods paragraph |
| `lvp` | log(37.8) L, held constant | Table III Vp = 37.8 L/70 kg, no RSE; same Methods paragraph |
| `e_wt_cl_q`, `e_wt_vc_vp` | 0.75, 1 (held constant) | Methods "Covariate Analysis" allometric equations; control stream `(BBWT/70)**0.75` and `(BBWT/70)` |
| Rhodin renal maturation | `PAGE^3.4 / (47.7^3.4 + PAGE^3.4)` | Methods "Covariate Analysis"; Table III equation; control stream `Fmat_egfr` |
| eGFR reference | 114.1 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (at full maturity) | Results CL equation and Table III equation; control stream `Fmat_egfr*114.1` |
| Febrile threshold | daily maximum >= 38 degC -> 1 | Table II and Table III footnotes |
| `etalcl` | omega^2 = 0.0963 | Table S3 'IIV CL' 0.0963; Table III 31.0% = sqrt(0.0963) (RSE 19.5%) |
| `propSd` | 0.303 | Table III residual proportional error 30.3% (RSE 20.0%); control stream `Y = F*(1+ERR(1))` |
| Two-compartment structure, IV input | n/a | Methods; control stream `ADVAN3 TRANS4`, `S1 = V1` |

The CL equation in full (Results, and the first row of Table III):

`CL = 6.50 * (WT/70)^0.75 * PAGE^2.17 / (49.1^2.17 + PAGE^2.17) * [CRCL / (Fmat_eGFR * 114.1)]^0.423 * 1.27^BODYTEMP_FEBRILE`

with `PAGE` the postmenstrual age in weeks and `CRCL` the modified-Schwartz
eGFR in mL/min/1.73 m^2.

# The packaged model reproduces the published clearance equation

The individual clearance is an algebraic output of the model, so a solve at a
set of covariate values must return exactly what the Table III equation gives
for the same values. The grid below spans the neonatal-to-adolescent range,
three renal-function levels and both temperature states.

```{r cl-equation}
mod <- readModelDb("Tanaka_2026_vancomycin")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod, "omega")

cl_published <- function(WT, PAGE, CRCL, febrile) {
  fmat <- PAGE^2.17 / (49.1^2.17 + PAGE^2.17)
  fmat_egfr <- PAGE^3.4 / (47.7^3.4 + PAGE^3.4)
  6.50 * (WT / 70)^0.75 * fmat * (CRCL / (fmat_egfr * 114.1))^0.423 * 1.27^febrile
}

grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  WT = c(4, 15, 45),
  PAGE = c(46, 120, 900),
  CRCL = c(60, 114.1, 180),
  BODYTEMP_FEBRILE = c(0, 1)
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())

ev_grid <- grid |>
  mutate(time = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")

# Typical values for many covariate sets at once: rxode2 warns that a
# multi-subject solve has no omega, which is the intent here.
cl_check <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_grid, returnType = "data.frame",
                  keep = c("WT", "PAGE", "CRCL", "BODYTEMP_FEBRILE")),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("multi-subject simulation without", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  }
) |>
  mutate(cl_eq = cl_published(WT, PAGE, CRCL, BODYTEMP_FEBRILE),
         rel_err = cl / cl_eq - 1)

# Algebraic output against its own closed form: pure floating-point error.
stopifnot(nrow(cl_check) == nrow(grid), max(abs(cl_check$rel_err)) < 1e-10)

# The febrile multiplier is exactly 1.27 for every covariate combination.
ratio <- cl_check |>
  select(WT, PAGE, CRCL, BODYTEMP_FEBRILE, cl) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = BODYTEMP_FEBRILE, values_from = cl, names_prefix = "bt") |>
  mutate(ratio = bt1 / bt0)
stopifnot(max(abs(ratio$ratio - 1.27)) < 1e-10)

cl_check |>
  filter(WT == 15, CRCL == 114.1) |>
  select(PAGE, BODYTEMP_FEBRILE, cl, cl_eq) |>
  dplyr::rename("PMA (weeks)" = PAGE, "BT >= 38 degC" = BODYTEMP_FEBRILE,
                "Model CL (L/h)" = cl, "Table III equation (L/h)" = cl_eq) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, caption = "Clearance for a 15 kg child at eGFR 114.1 mL/min/1.73 m^2.")
```

For an adult-sized reference subject (70 kg, fully matured) at an eGFR of
114.1 mL/min/1.73 m^2 the model returns 6.50 L/h afebrile and 8.26 L/h febrile,
the paper's theta_CL and theta_CL x theta_BT38.

## How clearance moves with age, renal function and fever

```{r cl-plots, fig.height = 4}
age_curve <- tibble::tibble(
  age_y = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 96, 108, 120, 132,
            144, 156, 168, 180, 192, 204) / 12,
  wt_med = c(3.0, 4.3, 5.5, 6.3, 7.7, 8.6, 9.2, 10.4, 11.8, 13.8, 15.8, 17.8,
             20.0, 22.5, 25.5, 28.5, 32.5, 37.0, 42.0, 46.5, 50.0, 52.5, 54.5, 56.0)
)
wt_for_age <- function(age_y) stats::approx(age_curve$age_y, age_curve$wt_med, xout = age_y, rule = 2)$y

profile_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  age_y = seq(1 / 12, 17.9, length.out = 120),
  CRCL = c(60, 120, 180),
  BODYTEMP_FEBRILE = c(0, 1)
) |>
  mutate(WT = wt_for_age(age_y), PAGE = age_y * 52.1775 + 40,
         cl_per_kg = cl_published(WT, PAGE, CRCL, BODYTEMP_FEBRILE) / WT,
         temp = ifelse(BODYTEMP_FEBRILE == 1, ">= 38 degC", "< 38 degC"))

ggplot(profile_grid, aes(age_y, cl_per_kg, colour = factor(CRCL), linetype = temp)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Postnatal age (years)", y = "Typical CL (L/h/kg)",
       colour = "eGFR\n(mL/min/1.73 m^2)", linetype = "Daily max BT",
       title = "Typical vancomycin clearance per kg by age, eGFR and fever",
       caption = "Weight from the maintainers' approximate Japanese median weight-for-age curve; term birth.")
```

Weight-normalised clearance peaks in early childhood, where the maturation term
is near complete but `(WT/70)^0.75 / WT` is still large, and falls through
adolescence. This is the shape behind Table IV's highest mg/kg doses in the
1 to <6 year group.

# Steady-state identity

At steady state the AUC over one dosing interval equals dose / CL whatever the
distribution parameters. PKNCA on a typical-value solve checks that the ODE
system, the infusion input and the clearance agree.

```{r ss-identity}
ss_subj <- data.frame(id = 1L, WT = 20, PAGE = 6 * 52.1775 + 40, CRCL = 120, BODYTEMP_FEBRILE = 0)
tau <- 6
ss_dose <- 15 * ss_subj$WT # 15 mg/kg q6h, 1-h infusion
ev_ss <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  ss_subj |> tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 234, by = tau)) |>
    mutate(amt = ss_dose, dur = 1, evid = 1, cmt = "central"),
  ss_subj |> tidyr::crossing(time = seq(228, 240, by = 0.05)) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_ss, returnType = "data.frame",
                          rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)
# A single-subject solve returns no `id` column.
conc_ss <- sim_ss |> filter(!is.na(Cc)) |> mutate(id = 1L, group = "typical") |> select(id, time, Cc, group)
dose_ss <- ev_ss |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(id, time, amt) |> mutate(group = "typical")
nca_ss <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_ss, Cc ~ time | group + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_ss, amt ~ time | group + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 234, end = 240, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE),
  options = list(auc.method = "linear")
))
auc_ss <- as.data.frame(nca_ss) |> filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |> pull(PPORRES)
cl_ss <- cl_published(ss_subj$WT, ss_subj$PAGE, ss_subj$CRCL, 0)
# Linear trapezoid on a 0.05-h grid: about 1e-4 relative error, from the
# curvature of the decline.
stopifnot(abs(auc_ss / (ss_dose / cl_ss) - 1) < 1e-3)
tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("PKNCA AUC over one interval at day 10 (ug*h/mL)", "Dose / CL (ug*h/mL)"),
  Value = c(auc_ss, ss_dose / cl_ss)
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "6-year-old, 20 kg, eGFR 120, afebrile, 15 mg/kg q6h.")
```

# Replicating Table IV: optimal daily doses

## Virtual cohort

Tanaka 2026 simulated each stratum from age- and sex-specific weight
distributions built from the Japanese year-2000 national growth survey LMS
tables (Isojima 2016), eGFR drawn uniformly within each band, and the final
model's population parameters, then computed AUC48-72h by the linear trapezoid
on a 0.25-h grid. The LMS tables are not reproduced in the paper, so the cohort
below uses the maintainers' approximate Japanese median weight-for-age curve
with 12% log-normal scatter (see Assumptions and deviations). Ages are uniform
within each age group and every child is assumed born at term, so postmenstrual
age is postnatal age plus 40 weeks (the paper assigned 280 days of gestation
where it was not recorded).

The dosing regimen inside a day is not stated either. The cohort receives the
daily dose as four 1-h infusions every 6 h. Because the model is linear, the
AUC of every subject is proportional to the dose, so one solve at a reference
daily dose of 10 mg/kg/day gives the AUC48-72h at any other dose by scaling.

There are 40 strata (5 age groups x 4 eGFR bands x 2 temperature states) with
100 virtual children each.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20261101)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261101)

age_groups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~age_group,           ~age_lo_y,  ~age_hi_y,
  "1 - < 3 months",      1 / 12,     3 / 12,
  "3 - < 12 months",     3 / 12,     1,
  "1 - < 6 years",       1,          6,
  "6 - < 12 years",      6,          12,
  "12 - < 18 years",     12,         18
)
egfr_bands <- tibble::tribble(
  ~egfr_band,   ~egfr_lo, ~egfr_hi,
  "50 to 79",   50,       80,
  "80 to 119",  80,       120,
  "120 to 159", 120,      160,
  "160 to 199", 160,      200
)
n_per_stratum <- 100L
ref_daily_mgkg <- 10

strata <- tidyr::crossing(age_groups, egfr_bands, BODYTEMP_FEBRILE = c(0, 1)) |>
  mutate(stratum = row_number())

cohort <- strata |>
  tidyr::uncount(n_per_stratum) |>
  mutate(
    id = row_number(),
    age_y = stats::runif(n(), age_lo_y, age_hi_y),
    WT = wt_for_age(age_y) * exp(stats::rnorm(n(), 0, 0.12)),
    PAGE = age_y * 52.1775 + 40,
    CRCL = stats::runif(n(), egfr_lo, egfr_hi)
  )
stopifnot(nrow(cohort) == 40L * n_per_stratum, !anyDuplicated(cohort$id))

dose_times <- seq(0, 66, by = 6)
ev_doses <- cohort |>
  select(id, WT, PAGE, CRCL, BODYTEMP_FEBRILE, stratum) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = dose_times) |>
  mutate(amt = ref_daily_mgkg * WT / 4, dur = 1, evid = 1, cmt = "central")
ev_obs <- cohort |>
  select(id, WT, PAGE, CRCL, BODYTEMP_FEBRILE, stratum) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = seq(48, 72, by = 0.25)) |>
  mutate(amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
ev_tab <- dplyr::bind_rows(ev_doses, ev_obs) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
```

## Simulation and AUC48-72h

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_tab, returnType = "data.frame",
                       keep = c("stratum"))
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$Cc))

conc <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, stratum)
dose_df <- ev_doses |> select(id, time, amt, stratum)

nca_obj <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | stratum + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | stratum + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 48, end = 72, auclast = TRUE),
  options = list(auc.method = "linear")
))
auc_ref <- as.data.frame(nca_obj) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(id, stratum, auc_ref = PPORRES)
stopifnot(nrow(auc_ref) == nrow(cohort), !anyNA(auc_ref$auc_ref))
```

## Dose search

For each stratum the dose in 5 mg/kg/day steps that maximises the proportion of
children with AUC48-72h between 400 and 600 ug*h/mL is selected, as in the
paper.

```{r dose-search}
dose_grid <- seq(5, 150, by = 5)
pta <- auc_ref |>
  tidyr::crossing(daily_mgkg = dose_grid) |>
  mutate(auc = auc_ref * daily_mgkg / ref_daily_mgkg) |>
  group_by(stratum, daily_mgkg) |>
  summarise(pta = 100 * mean(auc >= 400 & auc <= 600), .groups = "drop")

optimal <- pta |>
  group_by(stratum) |>
  slice_max(pta, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(strata, by = "stratum")

table4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~age_group,         ~BODYTEMP_FEBRILE, ~egfr_band,   ~paper_dose, ~paper_pta,
  "1 - < 3 months",   0, "50 to 79",   45, 49.8,
  "1 - < 3 months",   0, "80 to 119",  55, 48.4,
  "1 - < 3 months",   0, "120 to 159", 60, 49.6,
  "1 - < 3 months",   0, "160 to 199", 70, 48.8,
  "1 - < 3 months",   1, "50 to 79",   55, 50.0,
  "1 - < 3 months",   1, "80 to 119",  65, 49.0,
  "1 - < 3 months",   1, "120 to 159", 75, 49.0,
  "1 - < 3 months",   1, "160 to 199", 85, 48.4,
  "3 - < 12 months",  0, "50 to 79",   50, 47.8,
  "3 - < 12 months",  0, "80 to 119",  55, 48.3,
  "3 - < 12 months",  0, "120 to 159", 65, 48.5,
  "3 - < 12 months",  0, "160 to 199", 70, 48.4,
  "3 - < 12 months",  1, "50 to 79",   60, 48.6,
  "3 - < 12 months",  1, "80 to 119",  70, 47.7,
  "3 - < 12 months",  1, "120 to 159", 85, 48.1,
  "3 - < 12 months",  1, "160 to 199", 90, 48.6,
  "1 - < 6 years",    0, "50 to 79",   50, 49.8,
  "1 - < 6 years",    0, "80 to 119",  60, 48.8,
  "1 - < 6 years",    0, "120 to 159", 65, 48.8,
  "1 - < 6 years",    0, "160 to 199", 75, 49.0,
  "1 - < 6 years",    1, "50 to 79",   60, 48.2,
  "1 - < 6 years",    1, "80 to 119",  75, 48.8,
  "1 - < 6 years",    1, "120 to 159", 85, 49.1,
  "1 - < 6 years",    1, "160 to 199", 95, 48.3,
  "6 - < 12 years",   0, "50 to 79",   45, 48.7,
  "6 - < 12 years",   0, "80 to 119",  50, 47.6,
  "6 - < 12 years",   0, "120 to 159", 60, 48.2,
  "6 - < 12 years",   0, "160 to 199", 65, 47.1,
  "6 - < 12 years",   1, "50 to 79",   55, 48.3,
  "6 - < 12 years",   1, "80 to 119",  65, 48.0,
  "6 - < 12 years",   1, "120 to 159", 75, 47.4,
  "6 - < 12 years",   1, "160 to 199", 85, 47.7,
  "12 - < 18 years",  0, "50 to 79",   40, 50.1,
  "12 - < 18 years",  0, "80 to 119",  45, 51.6,
  "12 - < 18 years",  0, "120 to 159", 50, 49.5,
  "12 - < 18 years",  0, "160 to 199", 60, 49.1,
  "12 - < 18 years",  1, "50 to 79",   50, 48.8,
  "12 - < 18 years",  1, "80 to 119",  55, 49.0,
  "12 - < 18 years",  1, "120 to 159", 65, 49.3,
  "12 - < 18 years",  1, "160 to 199", 75, 49.5
)

cmp <- table4 |>
  inner_join(optimal, by = c("age_group", "egfr_band", "BODYTEMP_FEBRILE")) |>
  left_join(pta |> rename(paper_dose = daily_mgkg, pta_at_paper_dose = pta),
            by = c("stratum", "paper_dose")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (daily_mgkg / paper_dose - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(cmp) == 40L, !anyNA(cmp$pta_at_paper_dose))

# Structural: a mis-transcribed CL, exponent, unit or febrile factor moves
# every optimal dose by tens of percent. Envelope: the per-stratum optimum
# rides on a flat attainment curve and a 100-child cohort, so single cells
# can sit one or two 5-mg/kg steps from the paper's.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(cmp$pct_diff)) < 10,
  quantile(abs(cmp$pct_diff), 0.9) < 25,
  # At the paper's own doses about half the cohort should be in range
  # (paper 47-52%); 100-child binomial SE is 5 points.
  median(cmp$pta_at_paper_dose) > 35,
  median(cmp$pta_at_paper_dose) < 60
)

cmp |>
  mutate(temp = ifelse(BODYTEMP_FEBRILE == 1, ">= 38 degC", "< 38 degC")) |>
  arrange(match(age_group, age_groups$age_group), BODYTEMP_FEBRILE,
          match(egfr_band, egfr_bands$egfr_band)) |>
  select(age_group, temp, egfr_band, paper_dose, daily_mgkg, paper_pta,
         pta, pta_at_paper_dose) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Age" = age_group, "BT" = temp, "eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m^2)" = egfr_band,
    "Paper optimal dose (mg/kg/day)" = paper_dose,
    "Simulated optimal dose (mg/kg/day)" = daily_mgkg,
    "Paper attainment (%)" = paper_pta,
    "Simulated attainment at simulated optimum (%)" = pta,
    "Simulated attainment at paper dose (%)" = pta_at_paper_dose
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Replicates Table IV of Tanaka 2026.")
```

```{r table4-figure, fig.height = 5}
cmp |>
  mutate(temp = ifelse(BODYTEMP_FEBRILE == 1, ">= 38 degC", "< 38 degC"),
         age_group = factor(age_group, levels = age_groups$age_group),
         egfr_band = factor(egfr_band, levels = egfr_bands$egfr_band)) |>
  select(age_group, egfr_band, temp, Paper = paper_dose, Simulated = daily_mgkg) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Paper, Simulated), names_to = "source", values_to = "dose") |>
  ggplot(aes(egfr_band, dose, colour = temp, shape = source, group = interaction(temp, source))) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
  facet_wrap(~age_group, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "eGFR band (mL/min/1.73 m^2)", y = "Optimal daily dose (mg/kg/day)",
       colour = "Daily max BT", shape = NULL,
       title = "Optimal daily vancomycin dose: Table IV versus the packaged model") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

The fever ratio is the paper's headline clinical result. Febrile children need
1.2 to 1.3 times the afebrile dose in every stratum of Table IV; in the packaged
model the ratio of optimal doses is:

```{r fever-ratio}
fever_ratio <- cmp |>
  select(age_group, egfr_band, BODYTEMP_FEBRILE, daily_mgkg, paper_dose) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = BODYTEMP_FEBRILE, values_from = c(daily_mgkg, paper_dose)) |>
  mutate(sim_ratio = daily_mgkg_1 / daily_mgkg_0, paper_ratio = paper_dose_1 / paper_dose_0)
# Clearance ratio is exactly 1.27, so the dose ratio sits near it; the 5-mg/kg
# grid quantises single cells.
stopifnot(abs(median(fever_ratio$sim_ratio) - 1.27) < 0.1)
summary(fever_ratio[, c("paper_ratio", "sim_ratio")])
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Weight-for-age.** The paper drew weights from the LMS parameters of the
  Japanese year-2000 national growth survey (Isojima 2016), by sex. Those tables
  are not in the paper or its supplement. The virtual cohort uses an approximate
  sex-pooled Japanese median weight-for-age curve compiled by the maintainers,
  with 12% log-normal scatter. Dose per kg depends on weight only through
  `(WT/70)^0.75 / WT`, so a 10% error in a median weight shifts the optimal
  mg/kg dose by about 2.5%.
* **Term birth.** Every virtual child is assumed born at 40 weeks, so
  postmenstrual age is postnatal age plus 40 weeks; the paper did the same when
  gestational age was missing.
* **Within-day regimen.** The paper does not say how the simulated daily dose
  was divided or infused. Four 1-h infusions every 6 h were assumed. With linear
  elimination the AUC48-72h barely depends on the split.
* **Cohort size.** The paper used 10,000 subjects per stratum; this vignette
  uses 100 per stratum to keep the build fast. The attainment curve is flat near
  its maximum, so single strata can land one or two 5 mg/kg steps from the
  paper's optimum; the gates test the median and the 90th percentile of the
  difference, not each cell.
* **Residual error.** AUC48-72h is computed from individual predictions without
  residual error, as in the paper's dose-finding simulation.
* **Covariate coding.** The paper's `BT38` column is carried as the
  `BODYTEMP_FEBRILE` canonical (1 when the daily maximum body temperature is
  >= 38 degC). It is time-varying in the source data; supply one value per
  day. `PAGE` must be supplied in weeks.
* **Residual-error SD.** Table III prints 30.3%; supplement Table S3 lists the
  variance as 0.0912, whose square root is 0.302. The Table III value is used.
* **Published model code.** The supplement's control stream carries initial
  estimates; its structure (two-compartment `ADVAN3 TRANS4`, the `Fmat_egfr`
  adjustment, the `BT38` branch on clearance and the proportional error) agrees
  with the paper's equations, and the final values come from Table III.
* **Figures not reproduced.** Figure 1 (goodness of fit) and Figure 2
  (prediction-corrected VPC) need the observed data, which were not published.
* **No published NCA.** The paper reports no non-compartmental parameters, so
  there is no NCA comparison table; Table IV is the quantitative check.
